policies.note: Curtailments affect junior water rights holders when water is scarce. They are triggered by drought or water unavailability, not by agricultural revenue changes.

policies.policy_name: State and federal economic policy responses
policies.note: Revenue losses due to curtailments may activate economic support measures; changes in agricultural revenue track drought conditions but do not directly trigger curtailments.

policies.policy_name: Water for irrigation / water rights enforcement
policies.note: Curtailments follow constitutional water use priorities and rights, ensuring allocation aligns with seniority and scarcity conditions.
Direct producer grants, technical assistance, farm business management, financial planning, and marketing support are provided to farms affected by curtailed water deliveries.
Increased dependence on groundwater triggers reduced pumping or curtailment orders, fees, and potential land fallowing under local GSA authority.
Policies implemented in Tier 2 continue and are reinforced under more severe water scarcity conditions.

policies.policy_name: Curtailment, groundwater, and local water source management
policies.note: Unprecedented drought or catastrophic conditions result in full reliance on groundwater and local sources. Water supplies are heavily reduced and allocated only for basic human health, safety, and food security.
Emergency water planning measures are implemented to allocate scarce resources to critical human and food needs.
